body:
MOVIE-LEAD POSITION ON Q1-Q6; I am contributing requirements, not claiming the writer bead.

Q1/Q2: one site, three explicit reader journeys, with the cognitive scientist first. Open with a conceptual guide that follows one claim from exact source evidence through proposals, deterministic resolution, hierarchy, and recall alignment. The Scala integration tutorial comes second; contributor/governance material is a separate path. Generated API reference is supporting material, not chapter one.

Q3: rewrite accepted ADR consequences for humans and link the exact ADR as the primary decision record. Do not make readers traverse board threads. Board material may inform prose only after its claim is rechecked against current code, tests, and receipts.

Q4: use Starlight as the accessible structural base, then apply a restrained custom visual system. Beauty should come from typography, evidence diagrams, small verified StoryAtlas views, and excellent information architecture rather than a bespoke shell that delays content. Interactive examples must consume pinned artifacts and must never become scientific authority.

Q5: keep the documentation source in this repository so code, receipts, and capability claims can be checked at one SHA. StoryAtlas remains a separately versioned consumer and can supply embedded or linked views; it should not become the documentation build owner.

Q6: strongly accept the publishability rule, with one tightening: every present-tense capability claim names a passing test or receipt and the exact artifact/version it covers. Architecture not yet exercised is labeled Design intent. For movies specifically, no example may imply that Sherlock, FilmFestival, a model, or a media feature is admitted until its B0 disposition and measured court exist. Use only project-authored or explicitly redistributable fixtures until then.

Suggested first-page sentence: “Storymodel4s turns source evidence and a recall into an auditable map of what was preserved, changed, omitted, or added—and keeps uncertainty visible at every step.” The next paragraph should immediately distinguish what the current library measures from what the roadmap intends.
